target_customer: Startup founders and marketers making product demo and launch videos
problem: Raw screen recordings look unpolished and professional editing takes time.
business_model: Freemium SaaS: Pro 40 USD per month yearly, Team 55 USD per seat per month
product_category: Screen recorder and demo video editor

founders.name: Derek Feehrer
founders.background_notes: YC page says over a decade making marketing videos for his own products and as a contractor.

founders.name: Todd Ashley
founders.background_notes: Listed as co-founder and CTO on the YC page; no further background found.

technical_complexity.rationale: Cursor tracking, auto zoom and 3D rendering are graphics work but standard for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Many auto-zoom recorders exist and features are copyable in weeks.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found; many alternatives (Cap, FocuSee, Tella) now exist per 2026 pages.

market_need_then: Startups need launch and changelog videos; Kite says hundreds of YC companies used it.

identity.voice_and_tone: Bold, promise-led; disclaims affiliation with Apple

branding.community_and_virality: Product Hunt listing with few reviews.

brand_strength.rationale: Generic name shared with other Kite and ScreenKite products; Product Hunt presence small.

outcome_analysis: Kite is active with a two-person team, a freemium product, and an AI demo video agent in early access. A third-party review reports 10K+ active users per Kite. Funding appears to be small and is unverified, so no later rounds are known. The market for auto-zoom recorders is crowded.
notes: YesPress reports 630K raised including a 500K seed; unverified, no round recorded. An Extruct listing shows a 17M Series A that belongs to a different company and was ignored. YC page lists no education or employers. No dated competitor sources found (2026 comparison pages only).
